obligations.note: The change adds `if payee.category == "tax_authority": continue` to `purge_due` in payments/retention.py, so closed tax-authority payees keep their NPI past the approved 84-month period with no legal hold. RET-1 allows legal hold as the only exemption, and no approved policy value or exception permits a category carve-out.

The register has no exception for RET-1 or component payments.retention; its only entries are for SES-1 (expired), LOG-1 (mortgage.logging) and MFA-1 (withdrawn). The deviation therefore has no valid exception behind it.

Ticket CHG-26374 (standard) was approved by Erik Brandt (change_manager) at 2026-10-05T02:53Z, before the PR opened on 2026-10-06. Its components ['payments.retention'] cover the only touched path, apps/baseline-payments/payments/retention.py.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa@fernbrook.example, a payments change_approver. She is a different person from the author, Aisha Bello, under all of Bello's listed addresses.
The approval names the head commit 12376ec, which is the change's only commit, so nothing was added after it.

records/ci/run.json shows a successful payments run on head 12376ec. Its JUnit report has 172 tests with 0 failures and 0 skips, including the registered RET-1 control test test_sampled_purge_respects_hold. That test is labelled `sample` and uses only vendor payees, so it does not exercise the new tax_authority branch. I couldn't re-run the suite here because pytest isn't installed in the sandbox.

summary: PR-1222 makes the payments retention job skip closed payees in the tax_authority category, so their NPI is no longer purged after the approved 84-month retention period. RET-1 requires purging on schedule, with legal hold as the only exemption. No approved policy or registered exception covers this deviation, so RET-1 and EXC-1 are refuted. The process records (ticket, independent code review on the head commit, passing CI on the head commit) are in order, but CI only passes because the RET-1 control test is a vendor-only sample that never hits the new branch. The change is rejected.
